title: The eight-piece society orchestra and its instrumentation
summary: DeDroit gives the makeup of his society orchestra and when he enlarged it, praising trumpeter Al Hurt but noting he was too loud for carnival balls.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: When you had your society orchestra, you'd stick to Biloxi and so forth, a sort of society type of orchestra where you had a larger than a Dixieland group anyway. Oh yes.
We used eight men. Eight men? Yes. We used three saxes, two brass and three rhythm.
And one of the rhythm was a guitar or a banjo or? No, it was bass. Bass.

Bass drums, bass drums and piano. First and third alto and second tenor. Now sometimes if I could play for private, you see the country club, they were used to having eight men and they didn't want to spend, you know, they had so much to spend.

Yeah, yeah. But if I played for a convention or anything, I could almost exactly the number of men, you know, I could play for a Buick, I could get 15, and I'd use Al Hurt on first trumpet. But I couldn't use Hurt because he overpowered the band. I couldn't use him on carnival ball. It would sound like a trumpet solo. You know? He was a hard worker. He didn't have all this beard and everything like that. I used to call him, I used to call him, oh, I had a nickname. I said, about, he'd have been until he was fat. He was stout, with smooth complexion. But did he play the drums? Oh my. About too much. Prepare you try to use him. You know, Russ died. They have a little notice on the musician this month about Russ.
